questions.statement: The present ________ you gave me is fantastic!
questions.context: Identifying an object relative pronoun for things.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Present is not a person.
Correct! "That" (or "which") can be the object of the clause (you gave it).

questions.explanation:
En esta oración, "that" es el objeto del verbo "gave". Se refiere al regalo (the present).

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The person to ________ you were speaking is the manager.

options.feedback: Incorrect. After a preposition, "whom" is the correct formal form.
Correct! Formal object pronoun used after prepositions.

questions.explanation:
En inglés formal, después de una preposición (to, with, for), usamos "whom" en lugar de "who" para referirnos a personas que son el objeto de la acción.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which of these is a correct way to say: "The girl who I met yesterday"?

options.text: The girl that I met yesterday.
options.feedback: Correct, but there is a more complete answer.
Correct, but there is a more complete answer.

options.text: Both A and B are correct.
options.feedback: Correct! When the pronoun is the object, we can use "that" or omit it entirely.

questions.explanation:
En las oraciones especificativas (defining), si el pronombre relativo es el objeto (yo conocí a ella), podemos usar "who", "that" o simplemente no poner nada.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: In which sentence is the relative pronoun the **object**?

options.text: The man who lives here is a doctor.
The man (who) I saw here is a doctor.
options.feedback: Correct! "I" is the subject, "who" is the object of "saw".

options.text: The dog that barked is mine.
The woman who won is happy.

questions.explanation:
Para saber si un pronombre es objeto, mira si hay otro sujeto (yo, tú, Luis) inmediatamente después del pronombre. Si lo hay, el pronombre es el objeto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is the most natural in spoken English?
questions.context: Prepositions at the end of the clause.

options.text: The house in which I live is small.
The house I live in is small.
options.feedback: Correct! In spoken English, we often omit the pronoun and put the preposition at the end.

options.text: The house which I live is small.
The house who I live in is small.

questions.explanation:
En el habla cotidiana, es muy común "colgar" la preposición al final de la oración de relativo y omitir el pronombre si es el objeto.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The museum ________ we visited in Bogotá had amazing exhibits.

options.feedback: Correct! Standard relative pronoun for an object (the museum we visited).
Incorrect. "Where" would need a different structure (the museum where we saw the exhibits).

questions.explanation:
Usamos "that" o "which" para referirnos a lugares cuando funcionan como el objeto directo del verbo (nosotros visitamos *el museo*).

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
"Whom did you invite to the party?" (Formal)
"Who did you invite to the party?" (Informal)

Which statement is true?

options.text: Only the first one is correct.
Both are grammatically acceptable, but "whom" is specifically for the object position in formal writing.
options.feedback: Correct! B1 level requires recognizing "whom" for formal contexts.

questions.explanation:
Aunque "who" se usa casi siempre en el habla, el estudiante B1 debe saber que "whom" existe para funciones de objeto en textos académicos o formales.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
"The student **the teacher praised** was very proud."
Is this sentence correct without a relative pronoun?

options.text: Yes, because the relative pronoun is the object (the teacher praised *him*).
options.feedback: Correct! Pronouns can be omitted when they are the object.

options.text: Yes, but only in informal text.
options.feedback: Incorrect. It's common in formal text too.

questions.explanation:
La omisión del pronombre relativo ("contact clauses") es muy común en inglés y el estudiante debe ser capaz de reconocer la estructura oculta.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: This is the song ________ I was telling you ________.
questions.explanation:
Al usar oraciones de relativo, es fundamental mantener la preposición correcta que requiere el verbo principal (tell about, listen to, look for).

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Identify the error:
"The **movie (A)** that **we (B)** watched **it (C)** last night **was (D)** great."

options.feedback: Correct! Error found. The relative pronoun "that" already represents the movie. You cannot have "it" (the movie) again in the same clause.

questions.explanation:
Un error típico en B1 es repetir el pronombre de objeto (it, him, them) dentro de la oración de relativo. El pronombre relativo ya cumple esa función.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is best for a formal letter of recommendation?

options.text: He is a guy I worked with.
He is a professional with whom I have had the pleasure of working for three years.
options.feedback: Correct! Uses formal "whom" and places the preposition correctly for a high-level register.

options.text: He is the person that I worked with him.
He is a professional who I worked.

questions.explanation:
El manejo de la formalidad mediante la estructura "Preposición + Whom" es una señal de competencia avanzada en el nivel B1.

questions.statement:
"I spent hours searching for the document. Finally, I found the file. My boss had sent it to me last week. It was in my 'spam' folder."
Choose the best summary:
questions.context: Selecting the best summary of a search.

options.text: I finally found the document that my boss had sent last week in the spam folder.
options.feedback: Correct! It efficiently uses a relative clause to identify the document.

options.text: The document who the boss sent was in the spam.
I found the spam folder that it had the boss in it.
My boss is a document that I found.

questions.explanation: Resumir búsquedas y hallazgos requiere el uso de oraciones de relativo de objeto para ligar el ítem encontrado con su origen o descripción previa de manera compacta.
